LIMPOPO GANGS

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Suspects in Thoriso's murder are linked to violence in the past. Tonight on Carte Blanche, we ask: could Thoriso’s death have been avoided had the police clamped down on the notorious gang earlier?

Unique Selling Point:
The story has gripped the attention of the country and we add a unique perspective by profiling the gang, with mostly underage members, which has long been terrorising the community in the area.

Summary:
In February, social media was shocked and appalled at a video showing a group of youngsters kicking and dragging Thoriso Themane. Thoriso later died of his injuries. Following that video, it emerged that Thoriso’s attackers are children between the ages of 13 and 16 who are members of a gang known as the Madhura Squad.
The gang is made up of children who attend various schools in the Capricorn and Flora Park areas in Polokwane. The gang has a reputation for heavy drinking, assaults and generally keeping the community on its toes with their misbehaviour.
One of the gang members is the teenage son of a retired policeman and is implicated in a stabbing incident which happened in December 2018. He was charged for that attack but the victim’s family says the police did not prioritise the investigation until after the gang killed Thoriso.
We will profile the gang with a focus on their age, social media posts, and alcohol and drug influence. We also investigate the extent to which adults with criminal intent are allegedly influencing the behaviour of the youngsters in question. We also look at unanswered questions in the Thoriso investigation – outstanding arrests and the vast distance between the area in which Thoriso was first attacked and the park where he was eventually found after the attack.

Further information:
-The Polokwane Observer is a community newspaper that has been investigating the gang since 2018. Editor Yolande Nel has video footage of a previous attack by the same gang responsible for Thoriso’s murder.
-Yolande will share this footage, and the condition for that is that the Polokwane Observer be credited accordingly and that the footage is blurred to hide the identity of the underage attackers.
-She allocated the story to two journalists in her team, senior investigative journalist RC Myburgh and field reporter Endy Senyatsi, who have been working the investigation on the ground.

Press Release:


Limpopo Child Gangs
A video showing a group of youngsters kicking and dragging Thoriso Themane emerges, sending shockwaves throughout the country. Themane, a young man from Limpopo, never stood a chance against the group who beat him to death. But was this an isolated incident or the work of a violent gang of children? Carte Blanche investigates whether this is the same gang terrorising the community.
Producer: Ntokozo Miya
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


LIMPOPO GANGS SCRIPT – FINAL MIX

FOCUS - Underage suspects in the brutal murder of Thoriso Themane have been linked to other violent crimes in the past. We ask: could Thorisho’s death have been avoided had the police clamped down on the notorious gang earlier?

VO – It’s been a tumultuous start to the new school year, with a number of children reported to have been attacked or stabbed throughout the country.

In Gauteng this week, a teenager was stabbed and killed on his way to school in Mondeor, and 3 underage suspects were arrested.

In the Western Cape, at least 17 incidents of stabbings have been reported in the province’s schools.

But it was the viral video of the brutal attack on Thorisho Themane by a group of school children in Limpopo, which caused public outrage and revealed a violent underbelly in South African schools.

In February, the body of 28-year-old Thorisho was discovered on a quiet street in Flora Park in Polokwane. He’d been badly beaten, and had injuries to his head and chest.

Mahlapahlapana Themane, Thorisho’s father, says his family has not yet seen the video of his son’s final moments.
Mahlapahlapana Themane – Thorisho’s father

One other person came the next day to offer us that video. We said: no, we don’t want to see it because of the descriptions that they have detailed to us. We thought it would traumatise us.
VO – Thorisho’s attackers allegedly call themselves the ‘Madhura Squad’, a gang with adult members and others as young as thirteen.
Mahlapahlapana Themane – Thorisho’s father

It was a shock because you don’t expect people of that age to do such a thing. It is an indication that we are living in a sick society.
VO – Hundreds gathered to bid Thoriso farewell in an emotional send-off a week later.
LINK – The attack on Thoriso Themane was not the first by the ‘Madhura Squad’, and some say, had the police acted on earlier complaints about the gang, he might still be alive today.
VO – Investigative journalist for the Polokwane Observer, RC Myburgh, says in January, the paper received a video showing an earlier attack by the gang on an unidentified victim.
RC Myburgh – Polokwane Observer

The only thing that came with it was a warning or an alert that if the gang was not stopped, this might turn into somebody being killed.
VO – Thoriso was killed a month later.

Shortly thereafter, social media alerted police to a video of yet another earlier assault by the gang.

In the video, a young man runs to safety in a nearby minibus but the boys chasing him drag him out and start kicking him.
RC Myburgh – Polokwane Observer

I think they quickly responded in arresting the suspects in Thorisho’s case. But I don’t think there was a lot of effort from them in the previous cases.
VO – This mother’s identity is hidden to protect her teenage son. She says, in December last year, her son was stabbed by a gang member who happens to be the son of a former policeman.
‘Thelma’ - Victim’s mother – [please distort voice]

A lady called me and she called from the hospital, and said my son is in the hospital. The boy stabbed him with a knife right next to the lungs.I just said: my God, it’s in your hands. To my surprise, the suspect has opened a case against my son, that my son stabbed his finger.
VO – Her son was arrested and released later on the same day without explanation. and no arrests were made in connection with his attack.

She heard about Thorisho’s murder from her son.
‘Thelma’ - Victim’s mother – [please distort voice]

He told me that it was that boy who stabbed him, that killed a person.
Mac – So it is the same boy that killed Thorisho?
‘Thelma’ - Yes. And I remember telling Makgopo [please bleep over name] that if you do not do anything to this boy, this boy will kill somebody.
LINK – In the two weeks that followed Thoriso’s murder, ten suspects were arrested, including teenagers aged between 13 and 16.
VO – Formerly known as Pietersburg, the capital of the Limpopo province changed its name to Polokwane, which means ‘place of safety’.

The Flora Park suburb in which Thoriso grew up, and eventually lost his life, is a few minutes away from the Polokwane city centre. It is home to a middle class community and is littered with a number of former model c schools, which some of his attackers attended.

Two decades after the name change, residents say they do not feel safe.
‘Thelma’ - Victim’s mother – [please distort voice]

When these things started with these young boys, it’s trauma for everyone to walk at night,.
VO – The ‘Madhura Squad’ has a strong social media presence and members often flash wads of cash and booze on their pages.

It is not clear why they killed Thorisho, but hours after his death, the gang posted about the murder on Facebook – joking about going to jail and speaking openly about the fatal blows to his head.

In another post, someone with knowledge of the attack posted a message which read “I know what you did was wrong. Your intentions were not to murder Thoriso.”

The following day, while a camera was rolling, a boy who allegedly participated in the murder was asked about the incident at school.
UPSOUND VIDEO – blur face, school badge and tie

Voice behind camera: "Mfana ke gore o kwa botse ka gore o bolaile motho? (Do you feel happy that you killed a person?)
Boy: "Akere ke ya tseba Tyma yaka yena le ka se mo dire selo. (I know my father is untouchable.)
VO – The boy in the video is the 15 year-old-son of a retired police officer. He is a grade 9 pupil at a local school. In other reports, the father denied the implication that he is above the law.

Mbuyiselo Botha of the South African Men’s Forum says when in a gang, boys do things that they wouldn’t normally do on their own.
Mbuyiselo Botha – South African Men’s Forum

It is this deep sense of wanting to belong, a sense that I want to be seen that I am also part of the mainstream. That is the main reason why boys would get involved in things that ordinarily they would not get themselves involved in.
VO – Botha says children from middle-class families are often thought to be fragile by those from underprivileged backgrounds, and some resort to violence to show a tough side.
Mbuyiselo Botha – South African Men’s Forum

They don’t want to be seen as your ‘cheeseboys’. I may be in this prestigious school, I may be from a relatively well-off family but I don’t want to be ostracised. I don’t want to be thought as if that I am something out of the ordinary.
Mac – Or that I am soft?
Botha – Absolutely.
VO – Botha says the level of brutality displayed by child gangs is reflective of our past.
Mbuyiselo Botha – South African Men’s Forum

We come from an era where, during apartheid, when you were necklacing - all of these things were done in a mob. The young boys, some of them may not have been born but they know of the stories. They have been told. We’d be liars if we don’t go back and say: there is a history, there is a context to this violence in South Africa.
VO – Such violence among young children must be tackled head on, says Botha.
Mbuyiselo Botha – South African Men’s Forum

00:10:04:18 – It’s going to be important for our schools to get involved, our faith-based, your mosques, your churches, your temples, everybody, your traditional leaders: we can’t believe that in South Africa, this is normal. It can’t be normal.
VO – Polokwane residents marched to demand not only justice for Thorisho but also, the arrest of more suspects.

It is believed as many as 14 people participated in his attack.
UPSOUND

Resident march
VO - But SAPS General Nneke Ledwaba is satisfied with the progress of the investigation and says the community was instrumental in the arrests.
Nneke Ledwaba – SAPS

We are working very well with our community members. They are the very ones who have led us to the arrest of all the suspects in this case.
VO – Ledwaba denied allegations that the police dragged their feet on earlier complaints against the gang, particularly in the case involving the policeman’s son.
Nneke Ledwaba – SAPS

I understand that there was a case that was opened. It was an assault GBH. The investigation is still on. The son of that policeman has been arrested. He is also in custody as we are talking now.
LINK – Parents of the victims of the ‘Madhura Squad’ say it is now up to the courts to mete out justice for the gruesome attacks on their children.
Mahlapahlapana Themane – Thorisho’s father

Who could have taught them to kill, except us parents? So in one way or the other, as a society we have sown this thing and now, we are reaping.

I think that now that my son is gone, quick action should be taken against people like this so that another life is not lost.



Promos

Violence in school uniform – could the murder of Thorisho Themane have been prevented had the police clamped down on a brutal gang of Limpopo schoolchildren earlier?

Thorisho Themane was brutally killed by schoolkids in Limpopo, while a camera was rolling. What drives young children to commit such heinous crimes?

The recent scourge of horrific violence at schools, and by young learners, has left the country shocked and appalled. What drives children to act so brutally?

Mbuyiselo Botha – South African Men’s Forum It is this deep sense of wanting to belong, a sense that I want to be seen that I am also part of the mainstream. The young boys, some of them may not have been born but they know of the stories. They have been told. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Suspects in Thoriso's murder are linked to violence in the past. Tonight on Carte Blanche, we ask: could Thoriso’s death have been avoided had the police clamped down on the notorious gang earlier?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The story has gripped the attention of the country and we add a unique perspective by profiling the gang, with mostly underage members, which has long been terrorising the community in the area.
metadata.Summary: In February, social media was shocked and appalled at a video showing a group of youngsters kicking and dragging Thoriso Themane. Thoriso later died of his injuries. Following that video, it emerged that Thoriso’s attackers are children between the ages of 13 and 16 who are members of a gang known as the Madhura Squad. The gang is made up of children who attend various schools in the Capricorn and Flora Park areas in Polokwane. The gang has a reputation for heavy drinking, assaults and generally keeping the community on its toes with their misbehaviour. One of the gang members is the teenage son of a retired policeman and is implicated in a stabbing incident which happened in December 2018. He was charged for that attack but the victim’s family says the police did not prioritise the investigation until after the gang killed Thoriso. We will profile the gang with a focus on their age, social media posts, and alcohol and drug influence. We also investigate the extent to which adults with criminal intent are allegedly influencing the behaviour of the youngsters in question. We also look at unanswered questions in the Thoriso investigation – outstanding arrests and the vast distance between the area in which Thoriso was first attacked and the park where he was eventually found after the attack.
metadata.Further information: -The Polokwane Observer is a community newspaper that has been investigating the gang since 2018. Editor Yolande Nel has video footage of a previous attack by the same gang responsible for Thoriso’s murder. -Yolande will share this footage, and the condition for that is that the Polokwane Observer be credited accordingly and that the footage is blurred to hide the identity of the underage attackers. -She allocated the story to two journalists in her team, senior investigative journalist RC Myburgh and field reporter Endy Senyatsi, who have been working the investigation on the ground.
